turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on in, Aoife. Your mam with you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Uh, I nearly cancelled. I'm grand, this is probably nothing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): What brought you down, in your own words?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm just a bit tired. I work in the bookshop and it's been mad, that's all.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been wrecked for three months. Asleep on the couch before the news.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah mam. It's not three months. Two weeks if even. A bit tired, not wrecked.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, so the tiredness is why you came, and the length of it is somewhere between two weeks and three months. You don't agree, so I won't call it exact.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell him about the stairs. She stops halfway up to the flat, gasping.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I get a small bit winded if I leg it up. I am not gasping. She loves a drama.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): A little breathless hurrying upstairs, then. Any chest pain with that?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Periods. Are they heavy, or much as usual?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Normal. Not heavy. Same as always.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any craving for ice, err, or chewing on odd things?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Ice, yeah, a tray of cubes a day. It's only a habit. Umm, I couldn't tell you when that started.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough? And the tummy, bowels, all quiet?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough. Tummy's grand, bowels are fine.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ye came in soaked. Still bucketing out there, is it?
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Desperate. The bus didn't come and the Luas was jammed. We stood there twenty minutes.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): And a fella had the hurling blasting, Cork and Limerick, roaring. Rain was sideways on O'Connell Street. Couldn't hear a thing.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Limerick will walk it. Your uncle Pat and that scarf will be unbearable.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll leave the match there. Pulse is 88 beats a minute, blood pressure 110 over 72. Eyelids are pale. Chest is clear and the heart sounds are normal.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about food. Any meat or fish?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm vegetarian, strict enough. No meat, no fish, for years. Eggs, cheese, and lentils are what I live on. I'm not starving myself.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vegetarian for years, eggs and dairy still, grand. Do you smoke, or take a drink?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked. One glass of wine at the weekend.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets at the moment? Ever had a reaction to a medicine?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No tablets. No, never, not a reaction. I took amoxacillin last year, the penicillin one, for a chest infection, finished it, no bother.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nothing current, and that penicillin-type antibiotic was fine, so no drug allergy that you know of. I'll say it back. Tiredness for a spell you and your mam put differently, a bit winded on the stairs, ice chewing, periods normal, long-time vegetarian, pale eyelids.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Working impression is possible iron deficiency. I wouldn't rule out low B12 either, with the diet. That's not confirmed.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Sure. I still think I'm just tired from the shop.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm booking bloods now, full blood count, ferritin, B12 and folate. No iron tablets until those are back. For the food, more lentils, eggs, dark greens, and some orange or fruit in the same meal, it helps the iron. Come back in two weeks for the results.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine. If we're done I'll chance the rain.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): We're done. Mind how you go.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: FBC is booked, but indication 'tiredness and possible iron deficiency' is inferred, not fully stated.
bad.text: Full blood count (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=Tiredness and possible iron deficiency)

bad.reason: Folate is booked, but 'vegetarian diet and possible deficiency' as indication is not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Serum folate (type=laboratory, status=planned, requested_by=doctor, indication=Vegetarian diet and possible deficiency)

omissions.text: Doctor advised not to start iron tablets until the blood test results are back.
Patient reported chewing about a tray of ice cubes per day; this quantity/detail is not recorded.
Patient denied abdominal symptoms and specifically said bowels were fine ('Tummy's grand, bowels are fine').
Patient stated periods are normal/same as always, not just 'not heavy'.
Patient reported tolerance of amoxicillin/penicillin previously ('finished it, no bother'), supporting no known penicillin/drug allergy; this tolerance detail is not explicitly recorded.
